answer: At the falcon haven every nest is registered and yields one nestling a year. A claim settles only when this head raised that bird from the nestling, so its imprint binds to this head alone and no sibling can borrow it, and the mirror copy of the nest ledger keeps one nest from backing two claims. When the bird flies home to the hills the nest is spent for good. A farm's tenth head needs a tenth nest, and nests are fixed sites that capital cannot buy, so keepers stop releasing to an address that gathers rings.
